allergies.notes: Requires premedication protocol (prednisone + diphenhydramine) for any iodinated contrast study.

active_problems.condition: Coronary artery disease, status post CABG

surgical_history.findings: Inflamed, gangrenous appendix without perforation. Localized purulent peritonitis in the right lower quadrant.
surgical_history.pathology: Acute suppurative and gangrenous appendicitis. No malignancy.
surgical_history.follow_up: Wound healed by secondary intention; uneventful recovery.

surgical_history.indication: Symptomatic cholelithiasis with recurrent biliary colic; mild gallbladder wall thickening on US
surgical_history.findings: Chronically inflamed gallbladder containing multiple cholesterol stones (largest 1.4 cm). Cholangiogram negative for choledocholithiasis. No bile duct injury.
surgical_history.pathology: Chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis. No dysplasia or malignancy.
surgical_history.follow_up: Returned to baseline activity at 2 weeks. No post-cholecystectomy syndrome.

surgical_history.procedure: Open right inguinal hernia repair with mesh (Lichtenstein)
surgical_history.indication: Symptomatic right indirect inguinal hernia, reducible
surgical_history.approach: Open, Lichtenstein tension-free with polypropylene mesh
surgical_history.findings: Indirect hernia sac extending into the inguinal canal; no incarceration. Internal ring widened to 3 cm.
surgical_history.complications: Mild postoperative urinary retention requiring single in-and-out catheterization.
surgical_history.follow_up: No recurrence at 12-month follow-up. Mesh well incorporated on subsequent imaging.

surgical_history.procedure: Coronary artery bypass grafting x3 (LIMA to LAD; SVG to OM1; SVG to PDA)
surgical_history.indication: Three-vessel coronary artery disease with NSTEMI; LAD 90% proximal, LCx 80% mid, RCA 85% distal
surgical_history.approach: Median sternotomy, on-pump CPB, mild hypothermia (32 °C)
surgical_history.findings: Heavily calcified LAD; diffuse disease in LCx and RCA. Ejection fraction intraoperatively 45%. All grafts patent at completion.
surgical_history.complications: Postoperative atrial fibrillation on POD 2, converted with amiodarone. Sternal wound seroma (resolved with conservative management).
surgical_history.follow_up: Cardiac rehab completed 12 weeks. EF improved to 52% at 6 months.

surgical_history.procedure: CT-guided percutaneous biopsy, right upper lobe pulmonary nodule
surgical_history.indication: 8 mm spiculated RUL nodule with interval growth on surveillance CT
surgical_history.findings: Three core specimens obtained from the periphery of the nodule.
surgical_history.complications: Small (10%) right apical pneumothorax, observed without chest tube; iodinated contrast reaction during planning CT (severe bronchospasm) - allergy added to record.
surgical_history.pathology: Benign granulomatous inflammation with non-caseating granulomas. Special stains negative for AFB and fungal organisms.
surgical_history.follow_up: Pneumothorax resolved on 4-hour post-procedure imaging. Pulmonology follow-up; nodule monitored.

surgical_history.indication: End-stage primary osteoarthritis right knee, refractory to conservative management
surgical_history.implant: Zimmer Biomet Persona PS, size F femur / size 5 tibia, 10 mm polyethylene insert; cemented with Palacos
surgical_history.findings: Severe tricompartmental cartilage loss with eburnation; medial meniscal tear; mild varus deformity (5°) corrected intraoperatively.
surgical_history.complications: None intraoperative. Postoperative DVT prophylaxis with enoxaparin; no thromboembolic events.
surgical_history.follow_up: Excellent ROM at 6 weeks (0–115°). KOOS score improved from 38 (preop) to 81 (12 months).

surgical_history.indication: BPH with refractory LUTS, recurrent urinary retention, post-void residual >250 mL
surgical_history.findings: Prostate volume ~78 mL preop; trilobar enlargement with median lobe prominence. Smooth bladder mucosa; trabeculation grade 2.
surgical_history.complications: Transient post-op hematuria, resolved with continuous bladder irrigation x 24 hours.
surgical_history.pathology: Nodular prostatic hyperplasia. No high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia or carcinoma.
surgical_history.follow_up: Catheter removed POD 2; voiding trial successful. IPSS improved from 24 to 8 at 3 months.

imaging_history.technique: Real-time gray-scale ultrasound of the gallbladder, liver, biliary tree, pancreas, and right kidney.
imaging_history.findings: Gallbladder contains multiple mobile, shadowing echogenic foci, the largest measuring approximately 1.4 cm, consistent with cholelithiasis. Gallbladder wall measures 3 mm (mildly thickened). No pericholecystic fluid. Negative sonographic Murphy sign at time of exam. Common bile duct measures 5 mm (within normal limits). Liver parenchyma is homogeneous without focal lesion. Pancreatic head visualized and unremarkable.
impression: Cholelithiasis with mild gallbladder wall thickening, suggestive of chronic cholecystitis.
No sonographic evidence of acute cholecystitis at this time.
Normal common bile duct caliber.

imaging_history.indication: NSTEMI; troponin peak 4.8 ng/mL; new T-wave inversions in V3–V6.
imaging_history.technique: Right radial access; selective left and right coronary angiography in standard projections; left ventriculography deferred due to renal function.
imaging_history.findings: Left main: minimal disease. LAD: 90% proximal stenosis with TIMI 2 flow. LCx: 80% mid-vessel stenosis. OM1 with 60% ostial disease. RCA: dominant; 85% stenosis in distal segment with TIMI 3 flow. No thrombus. Mild diffuse disease throughout.
impression: Severe three-vessel coronary artery disease.
Recommendation: surgical revascularization (CABG).

imaging_history.indication: Routine 1-year post-CABG follow-up; no acute symptoms.
imaging_history.technique: PA and lateral views of the chest.
imaging_history.findings: Median sternotomy wires intact and aligned. Mediastinal contour normal for postoperative state. Heart size top-normal. Lungs are clear without focal consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax. No pleural-based lesions. Bony thorax otherwise unremarkable. Surgical clips along the left internal mammary artery course.
impression: Stable post-CABG appearance.
No acute cardiopulmonary process.

imaging_history.indication: Lung cancer screening; 25 pack-year history, age 56, former smoker.
imaging_history.technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest from thoracic inlet to upper abdomen, 1.0 mm reconstructions, no IV contrast.
imaging_history.findings: An 8 mm spiculated nodule is identified in the apical segment of the right upper lobe (series 3, image 42), increased from 5 mm on the prior outside study from 2017-08. No additional pulmonary nodules. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy by size criteria. Mild centrilobular emphysema, predominantly upper lobes. Median sternotomy and CABG clips noted. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
impression: 8 mm spiculated right upper lobe nodule with interval growth — Lung-RADS 4B.
Recommend tissue sampling (PET/CT or CT-guided biopsy).
imaging_history.follow_up: PET/CT performed; subsequent CT-guided biopsy SX-005.

imaging_history.indication: Characterization of growing RUL pulmonary nodule.
imaging_history.technique: Whole-body PET/CT 60 minutes after IV administration of 10 mCi 18F-FDG. Blood glucose 118 mg/dL.
imaging_history.findings: RUL spiculated nodule measures 8 mm with mild FDG uptake (SUVmax 2.4), nonspecific. No hypermetabolic mediastinal, hilar, or supraclavicular adenopathy. No FDG-avid distant lesion. Mildly FDG-avid sigmoid focus (SUVmax 4.1) likely physiologic; correlate with colonoscopy as clinically indicated.
impression: RUL nodule with low-level FDG uptake — indeterminate; tissue sampling recommended.
Incidental sigmoid focal uptake — recommend correlation with colonoscopy.

imaging_history.indication: Post-procedure following CT-guided RUL nodule biopsy (SX-005).
imaging_history.findings: Small (~10%) right apical pneumothorax. Tract of biopsy needle visible with mild adjacent ground-glass hemorrhage in the RUL. No pneumomediastinum. No expanding hematoma. No left-sided pneumothorax.
impression: Small right apical pneumothorax post-biopsy, no chest tube indicated.
Expected post-biopsy intraparenchymal hemorrhage.

imaging_history.indication: Persistent right knee pain with mechanical symptoms; refractory to PT and intra-articular injections.
imaging_history.technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the right knee at 1.5 T including PD fat-sat, T2, T1, and STIR sequences. No IV contrast.
imaging_history.findings: Severe full-thickness chondral loss in the medial tibiofemoral compartment with subchondral marrow edema and a 1.2 cm subchondral cyst in the medial tibial plateau. Complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending to the inferior articular surface. Moderate joint effusion with synovitis. Patellofemoral compartment shows grade 3 chondromalacia and small Baker's cyst measuring 2.4 × 1.0 cm. ACL and PCL intact. Collateral ligaments intact.
impression: Severe medial compartment osteoarthritis with full-thickness cartilage loss and meniscal tear.
Moderate-grade patellofemoral chondromalacia.
Likely candidate for surgical management given severity and prior failed conservative care.

imaging_history.indication: Rising creatinine (1.5 mg/dL) and elevated PVR; evaluate for obstructive uropathy.
imaging_history.findings: Right kidney measures 11.2 cm; left kidney 11.0 cm. No hydronephrosis or nephrolithiasis. Cortical thickness preserved bilaterally. Bladder is markedly distended pre-void (volume ~520 mL). Prostate enlarged with median lobe protrusion, estimated volume 78 mL. Post-void residual 285 mL.
impression: No hydronephrosis.
Markedly elevated post-void residual with prostatomegaly and median lobe component — consistent with obstructive BPH.

imaging_history.technique: Standing AP, lateral, sunrise, and Rosenberg views.
imaging_history.findings: Bone-on-bone narrowing of the medial tibiofemoral compartment with subchondral sclerosis and large medial osteophytes. Mild lateral compartment narrowing. Patellofemoral joint with moderate narrowing and osteophytosis. Mild varus alignment (~5°). No fracture or lytic lesion.
impression: Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritis, medial-predominant, with mild varus deformity.
Findings support indication for total knee arthroplasty.

imaging_history.indication: Annual lung cancer screening; surveillance of known RUL biopsy-proven granuloma.
imaging_history.findings: RUL apical nodule measures 7 mm, stable to mildly decreased compared with 2021 study (was 8 mm). No new pulmonary nodules. No adenopathy. Stable centrilobular emphysema. Postsurgical changes from CABG unchanged.
impression: Stable RUL nodule, consistent with previously biopsied granuloma — Lung-RADS 2.
Continue annual screening.

imaging_history.indication: Pre-TURP planning; rule out clinically significant prostate cancer (PSA 6.2 ng/mL).
imaging_history.technique: 3 T multiparametric MRI of the prostate including T2WI, DWI (b values 50, 800, 1400, 2000), and DCE.
imaging_history.findings: Prostate volume 78 mL. Marked transition zone enlargement with heterogeneous BPH nodules. No discrete focal lesion in the peripheral zone. No restricted diffusion or suspicious early enhancement. Seminal vesicles symmetric, no invasion. No lymphadenopathy. Bladder wall mildly thickened with trabeculation.
impression: PI-RADS 2 — clinically significant prostate cancer is unlikely.
Markedly enlarged prostate with median lobe component, consistent with BPH.

imaging_history.body_part: Abdomen and pelvis, with oral contrast (no IV contrast given iodine allergy and CKD)
imaging_history.indication: Acute LLQ abdominal pain x 24 hours with low-grade fever; rule out diverticulitis.
imaging_history.technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis with oral contrast only.
imaging_history.findings: Sigmoid colon shows mural thickening over a 6 cm segment with associated mesenteric fat stranding and several diverticula. No pneumoperitoneum, abscess, or extraluminal contrast. Small adjacent reactive lymph node (8 mm short axis). Rest of the colon unremarkable. Postsurgical changes from cholecystectomy and inguinal hernia mesh repair noted, stable. Mild bilateral renal cortical thinning consistent with known CKD; no hydronephrosis. Bladder postsurgical from prior TURP. Aortoiliac calcifications without aneurysm. No free fluid.
impression: Acute uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis (Hinchey Ia).
No abscess or perforation.
Recommend outpatient antibiotic therapy and interval colonoscopy after resolution.
